findings:
## Problem

When observation-watcher invokes Claude Code, there is currently no requirement for Claude Code to produce a run report or sync its work to git. This means:

- We cannot audit what Claude Code did in response to an observation
- File edits may sit uncommitted locally with no record of what changed
- There is no ISO-timestamped artifact we can review or roll back to
- The feedback loop is effectively a black box after observation-watcher fires

## Required Changes to observation-watcher

The Claude Code prompt that observation-watcher constructs and passes must include the following mandatory instructions:

### 1. Write a full run report
At the end of every run, Claude Code must write a report file to:

  var/claude-code/runs/YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.json

File name must be ISO 8601 date string with **second granularity** (e.g. `2026-05-31T20:45:32.json`). No milliseconds, no UTC Z suffix in the filename — just the local ISO second string so filenames sort correctly.

The report must include:
- `observation_summary` — the one-line summary from the observation it acted on
- `observation_timestamp` — when the observation was written
- `run_started_at` — when Claude Code began
- `run_completed_at` — when Claude Code finished
- `files_changed` — array of file paths that were modified, created, or deleted
- `actions_taken` — plain-English description of every edit made and why
- `git_commit_hash` — the hash of the commit made at end of run (see below)
- `exit_status` — "success" | "partial" | "failed"
- `notes` — any caveats, skipped steps, or follow-up recommendations

### 2. Full git sync at end of every run
After writing the report, Claude Code must:
1. `git add -A` — stage all changed files including the run report itself
2. `git commit -m "claude-code: <observation_summary> [<ISO timestamp>]"` — commit message must include the observation summary and timestamp
3. `git push` — push to origin

The run report file must be included in this commit so the git history contains a full audit trail.

### 3. Never skip the sync
The git sync is not optional. If `git push` fails, Claude Code must log the failure in the report under `notes` and retry once. If it still fails, exit_status must be "partial" not "success".

## Why this matters
Without this, the autonomous loop has no accountability. We cannot tell from the outside whether Claude Code ran, what it changed, or whether its changes were preserved. The ISO-timestamped report + git sync gives us a complete, reviewable audit trail for every autonomous action.

---
## Mandatory Reporting and Git Sync Requirements

At the end of this run you MUST:

1. Write a run report to var/claude-code/runs/YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.json (ISO date, second granularity, e.g. 2026-05-31T20:45:32.json) containing: observation_summary, observation_timestamp, run_started_at, run_completed_at, files_changed (array), actions_taken (plain English), git_commit_hash, exit_status (success|partial|failed), notes.

2. Run: git add -A && git commit -m "claude-code: {observation_summary} [{ISO timestamp}]" && git push

---

This text must be appended to every prompt observation-watcher sends to Claude Code, regardless of the observation content.
summary: observation-watcher must inject full reporting and git sync requirements into the Claude Code prompt
